agree.reason: The sales record and the $12,500 comparison make a credible case, but the email asks for $2,500 over a $9,000 budget and gives nothing back, even though the writer had sketches in six weeks, final art by September 1 and two free marketing spots to offer, so an editor with an $8,000 option may well stall.

honest.reason: Every figure traces to the brief, and the email rightly drops the unsupported claim that every other publisher pays at least $12,000; 'well above $9,000' is a slight stretch given the range starts at $11,000.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly places $11,500 in the lower half of the agent's range and notes that the fee has stayed flat over six books, but it never works the numbers further, such as $9,000 over four months coming to about $2,250 a month or $11,500 being $1,000 under what another publisher actually paid.

right_comparison.reason: It compares her fee with outside rates, but not with the editor's real alternative: an untested illustrator at $8,000 against an illustrator whose list includes a state-reading-list title now in its fourth printing.

qualification.reason: The email is a straightforward request and needs no hedged forecast or condition.

objections.reason: The resisting editor's objections, a fixed $9,000 budget and a cheaper newer illustrator, go unanswered; the offer to send supporting material for approval helps a little, but the email gives no reason a proven illustrator is worth the extra cost.

fit.reason: It is a polite email of about 210 words, but it uses a '[Your name]' placeholder although her name was available, a generic subject line, never names The Night Garden, and ignores the end-of-next-week reply deadline.
